question.text: In portfolio assessment during AIF DD, 'vintage diversification' refers to:

answer.text: Investing in companies of different ages
Spreading investments across different fund vintage years to reduce timing risk

explanation.text: The Logic: In private-markets portfolio construction, "vintage diversification" refers to spreading commitments across funds of different vintage years so that capital deployment and entry-valuation exposure are distributed across multiple market cycles. This reduces the risk that the entire portfolio is anchored to a single market peak or trough. The Trap: Vintage diversification is not about the ages of underlying portfolio companies, has nothing to do with wine vintages or geographies, and is not about investing in antique asset classes — it is purely a time-diversification concept across fund vintage years. Note: The Series XIX-A AIF (Category I and II) Distributors workbook pages reviewed define vintage year, note timing effects on returns and entry valuations, and describe benchmarks by vintage year, but do not explicitly describe "vintage diversification" as spreading commitments across multiple vintages to reduce timing risk. The framing above reflects general private-markets practice rather than a workbook citation.
